mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form "the difference between the number of X and Y" as the signed subtraction X − Y, preserving the order of the names, not as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions "the difference between the number of ... and ..." in a peach/grape puzzle.
mathgap.example: Treating "the difference between Alice's and Bob's oranges" as |Alice − Bob| instead of Alice − Bob.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like "A has N more (or fewer) items than B" into the equation A = B + N (or A = B − N), handling combined forms that mention multiple comparisons.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering "has N more than" or "has N fewer than" phrasing.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "Taylor has 5 more oranges than Adolfo" as Taylor = Adolfo + 5, but mistakenly discarding solutions where the result would be negative.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement "A has N items" appears, set A’s current count to N at that moment, overwriting any previous value; later transfers may change it.
mathgap.example: Assuming a later statement "A has N items" fixes A’s count forever and ignoring subsequent transfers that change A’s amount.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the given order; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later relational statement, so that later equations see the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement appears before a relational statement involving the same persons.
mathgap.example: Delaying a transfer until after all other statements, causing a later relational equation to use stale counts.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order on each side; do not collapse to a single‑variable assignment.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering "the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have."
mathgap.example: Misreading "(A - B) = (C - D)" as "A = C - D" and dropping B.

mathgap.title: Switch (Swap)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons "switch" or "exchange" their items, exchange their current counts without altering the total number of items.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A and B switch their oranges" as both keeping their original counts instead of swapping them.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person "eats N" of an item, subtract N from their count; when it says they "multiply" or "double" their items, apply the arithmetic operation to their current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: On consumption, addition, subtraction, or multiplication statements.
mathgap.example: Forgetting to subtract the eaten amount from the person's count.

mathgap.title: Temporal Snapshot for Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Treat each relational statement as a constraint on the counts at the moment it appears; later changes (e.g., transfers) do not retroactively alter that constraint.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing any relational equation after earlier statements.
mathgap.example: Adjusting a previously satisfied difference equality after a later transfer, thereby violating the snapshot rule.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer of All Items
mathgap.principle: If a transfer statement says a person gives all their items to another, set the giver’s count to zero and add that amount to the receiver immediately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer phrase includes "all" or "everything".
mathgap.example: Misinterpreting "X gives all oranges to Y" as a fixed‑number transfer rather than moving the entire current amount.

mathgap.title: Complete Statement Extraction
mathgap.principle: Extract every statement about the target item (direct counts, differences, transfers, equality of differences) and translate each into an equation before solving; missing any statement leaves the system underdetermined and leads to incorrect answers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a mathgap problem, before any algebraic manipulation.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a transfer statement or stopping after a few equations and guessing the answer.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The word “difference” is often colloquially taken to mean magnitude, causing loss of sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two names and translate to X − Y, preserving sign.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model treats transfers as separate from the timeline, forgetting that later equations need the updated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process statements sequentially; when a transfer appears, update giver and receiver counts before any subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Belief that “has N items” sets a static baseline that never changes.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize that direct counts set the current count at that moment; later transfers can modify it.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Over‑simplifying “(A − B) = (C − D)” to “A = C − D”.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate the whole equality preserving both differences: (A − B) = (C − D).

mathgap.description: Incomplete processing of problem statements: stopping after a subset of constraints or ignoring many statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model may assume early deductions are sufficient or run out of time/space, leading to an underdetermined system.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Systematically parse the entire problem, extract every relevant statement, and include all resulting equations before solving.
